{{recipe}} 

Slow cooking makes already-tender pork chops melt-in-your-mouth tender.

== Ingredients ==
* 4 thick cut [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] rib chops
* [[Cookbook:Chop Rub|Chop rub]]
* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]]
* 8 dried [[Cookbook:Apple|apple]] rings
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] apple [[Cookbook:Cider Vinegar|cider vinegar]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] white [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|Worcestershire sauce]]
* 2 tbsp firmly packed dark [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]

== Procedure ==
#[[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] chops with olive oil and season liberally with chop rub. Set aside.
#Heat a large stainless steel or cast iron [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] over high heat. Add pork chops and cook until browned and slightly charred on both sides.
#Remove and set aside.
#Place pan back on heat and [[Cookbook:Deglazing|deglaze]] with white wine. Pour out wine and reserve.
#Place apples in the bottom of a [[Cookbook:Slow Cooker|crockpot]]. Place pork chops on top and drizzle with remaining ingredients.
#Cook on low 7–8 hours.
#Drain apples and pork into a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. Bring liquid to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] over high heat until reduced by half.
#Pour liquid back over pork chops and serve warm.
